## Decision record

_Every decision taken, with why. Newest last._

Add an entry when the question is settled, not when the answer is built —
`status` says how far it has got. A number is a
**stable identifier** and is never reused: an entry that turned out to record a
narrative rather than a foreclosure is withdrawn, and its number stays a hole
at the foot of this page.

**This page routes and does not restate.** An entry *is* its assertion file,
named for its number, so a conversation reaches one as
`@.meta/assertions/decisions/DR-001.yaml`. The line here says an entry exists
and what question it answered; only the entry is sufficient to apply it.

| [DR-330](assertions/decisions/DR-330.yaml) | A docstring is prose: every file a portfolio copies is held to the citation form, whatever its suffix | Adopted |
| [DR-331](assertions/decisions/DR-331.yaml) | A citation's claim is checked in the shapes a string search reaches, and nowhere else | Adopted |
| [DR-332](assertions/decisions/DR-332.yaml) | A gate is a predicate a re-run cannot overturn, so a citation's reading is a step that blocks nothing | Adopted |
| [DR-333](assertions/decisions/DR-333.yaml) | Schemas and executable tooling remain in scaffold inheritance, and APM is reserved for cognitive primitives | Adopted |
| [DR-334](assertions/decisions/DR-334.yaml) | Reader-facing literate programming rubric: a docstring states what to do, and argues with nobody | Adopted |
| [DR-335](assertions/decisions/DR-335.yaml) | The Ubiquitous Language regime: a 1:1 wiki parity check, and the second seat's judgement on unlinked domain nouns | Adopted |
| [DR-336](assertions/decisions/DR-336.yaml) | Dereference scopes a branch to the ground it moved, and whole-corpus citation upkeep belongs to the technical writer with retrieval | Adopted |
| [DR-337](assertions/decisions/DR-337.yaml) | Layered technical writing standard and in-memory BM25F record retrieval skill | Adopted |
| [DR-338](assertions/decisions/DR-338.yaml) | Concept is the atomic unit of domain meaning, and search indexes a concept's labels and definition | Adopted |
| [DR-339](assertions/decisions/DR-339.yaml) | Two-regime technical writing: the conversational register versus durable Diátaxis authoring | Adopted |
| [DR-340](assertions/decisions/DR-340.yaml) | A Persona compiles to an agent that answers as the Persona, for goal-directed collaborative design | Adopted |
| [DR-341](assertions/decisions/DR-341.yaml) | Inherited probes and the search benchmark generalise over what a portfolio holds, so a fresh specialization passes its gate | Adopted |
| [DR-342](assertions/decisions/DR-342.yaml) | The probes are a package under `.meta/checks/probes/`, one module per subject under test, with the harness apart | Adopted |
| [DR-343](assertions/decisions/DR-343.yaml) | The rule its instances share is stated as an Article of its own | Adopted |
| [DR-344](assertions/decisions/DR-344.yaml) | A script under .meta/ keeps its path as the entry point and its body lives in .meta/lib/<script>/, whose modules import each other as modules | Adopted |
| [DR-345](assertions/decisions/DR-345.yaml) | A module under .meta/ that is imported rather than run becomes a package of its own name in place, whose __init__ registers what its modules define | Adopted |
| [DR-346](assertions/decisions/DR-346.yaml) | Observed Failure covers Claims as well as guardrails, and Article 23 holds the author to checking one | Adopted |
| [DR-347](assertions/decisions/DR-347.yaml) | Specialization is tested end to end in a scratch repository with pre-judged portfolio fixtures | Adopted |
| [DR-348](assertions/decisions/DR-348.yaml) | A shell script or a recipe never hands Python its code inline | Adopted |
| [DR-349](assertions/decisions/DR-349.yaml) | Root recipes take only flags, subcommands and atomic identifiers, and a tool that takes prose is reached through a skill | Adopted |
| [DR-350](assertions/decisions/DR-350.yaml) | Mutation testing in both seed gates defaults to at most eight workers, with an override each | Adopted |
| [DR-351](assertions/decisions/DR-351.yaml) | Tooling shebangs keep python3, and Python 3.13 is asserted at the front door | Adopted |
| [DR-352](assertions/decisions/DR-352.yaml) | The Journaling Discipline is renamed Routing | Adopted |
| [DR-353](assertions/decisions/DR-353.yaml) | `just audit` compares a Project's gate with a bootstrap by step name and report shape, and prints each gap as an Issue | Adopted |
| [DR-354](assertions/decisions/DR-354.yaml) | A seat may not signal processes by name or number, because the sandbox does not confine signals | Adopted |
| [DR-355](assertions/decisions/DR-355.yaml) | Prose cites code by its path and the name of the thing in it, never by line number | Adopted |
| [DR-356](assertions/decisions/DR-356.yaml) | A Bootstrap exempts a Discipline whose subject its Projects do not hold | Adopted |
| [DR-357](assertions/decisions/DR-357.yaml) | Keys reach the supervisor's landing gate, by the names `main` declares, and never a seat | Adopted |
| [DR-358](assertions/decisions/DR-358.yaml) | `just audit --repository` audits a Project another repository asserts, running its gate from that repository's root | Adopted |
| [DR-359](assertions/decisions/DR-359.yaml) | `just audit` reads a gate that exits non-zero before reporting a step as having failed to run, prints no Issue, and exits 2 | Adopted |
| [DR-360](assertions/decisions/DR-360.yaml) | A seed Project's gate renders the seed as `acme` and gates the copy | Adopted |
| [DR-361](assertions/decisions/DR-361.yaml) | The Python seed's gate checks each wheel's `packages` against the tree, without building the wheel | Adopted |

## Holes

Numbers that were issued and are not decisions. They are never reused, and
the prose is kept: a paragraph that was worth writing does not stop being
true because it turned out to foreclose nothing.

- [DR-036](assertions/decisions/DR-036.yaml) — withdrawn. An audit report.
- [DR-045](assertions/decisions/DR-045.yaml) — withdrawn. A run report.
- [DR-084](assertions/decisions/DR-084.yaml) — withdrawn. It made a Decision name the Challenge it served so that `render.py --landed` could render what landed, as a step of PR First before merging.
- [DR-132](assertions/decisions/DR-132.yaml) — withdrawn. It decided the form of a GitHub Issue number (`#nn`) cited in inherited files, and gave resolving that number to the checker that reached GitHub.
- [DR-146](assertions/decisions/DR-146.yaml) — withdrawn. The change proposing this decision was superseded by DR-152.
- [DR-154](assertions/decisions/DR-154.yaml) — withdrawn. Its falsifier said "prose that stops citing counts at all retires this: the table empties, `counted()` fills nothing, and both come out", and that is met.
- [DR-222](assertions/decisions/DR-222.yaml) — withdrawn. It had only the developer adopt a decision, and a pull request carrying one wait for it, as steps of Written Decisions.
